sources_considered.why: Primary scaling study comparing models trained on the same dataset for the same token count.
OpenAI documents both GPT-4 improvements and continuing factual, reasoning and safety limitations.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4.3, Performance Improvements with Scale, Figure of Speech Detection example
evidence_items.explanation: Comparisons within the Gopher family hold the dataset and token count fixed and show that increasing parameters and training compute improved many tasks. This supports the gains component but cannot establish that every broader problem remained unsolved in March 2024.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5, Limitations; related safety results in Section 6
evidence_items.explanation: The report documents continuing factual and reasoning failures, and says safeguards can still be bypassed. It also reports substantial safety gains, including toxic-generation rates of 0.73% versus 6.48% for GPT-3.5 on its stated benchmark; these combined interventions do not isolate scaling.

unresolved_gaps: The records do not cover every broader challenge referred to by any of the problems above.
No agreed application-level threshold establishes when each problem counts as solved.
GPT-4's combined training and safety changes do not isolate the effect of scaling.
The cited scaling and model reports are earlier results, not a comprehensive inventory of the strongest systems at the post date.
